description: A streaming event producer must give final approval for an interactive fan-voting finale during a live awards stream and lock the voting rules, channel, capacity, and moderation plan.

shared_context.S1: The awards stream is scheduled for Saturday at 8:00 PM and includes a proposed live fan-voting finale.
shared_context.S2: Mara gives the binding final approval for the finale plan.
shared_context.S3: The audience technology team estimates that as many as 15,000 remote viewers may try to participate.
shared_context.S4: At the final greenlight meeting, the broadcast standards producer and audience technology lead state their confirmed requirements and current provisions, and Mara locks the plan using those constraints; no additional vendor response or document-entry step is required before approval.

PF1.text: Devon confirmed in the broadcaster's standards memo that the vote may run only with an under-18 exclusion and must close at exactly 9:40 PM so the result can be reviewed before the closing credits; these confirmed requirements are ready to be adopted directly into the final plan.

PF2.text: Riley confirmed with the voting vendor that Saturday's provisioned service supports web voting reached through an on-screen QR code, not SMS voting, and is capped at exactly 12,000 eligible voters; these current provisions are sufficient to set the final channel and cap, with audience messaging covering the limit.

acceptance_conditions: The fan vote must be enabled under a compliant operating plan.
Voting must close at exactly 9:40 PM.
Voting must use the provisioned web channel reached through an on-screen QR code.
The plan must cap eligible voters at exactly 12,000.
An age-gate commitment must be recorded.
A QR web-voting commitment must be recorded.

decisive_facts.why: The standards memo changes eligibility to '18 and older only,' fixes the vote close at exactly 9:40 PM, and requires the age-gate commitment.
The vendor confirmation changes the channel to web via an on-screen QR code, fixes the eligible-voter cap at exactly 12,000, and requires the QR web-voting commitment.
